elements.element: Vendor has a duty to defend against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 states that HDI shall “defend” against any covered third-party claim.

elements.element: Vendor has a duty to indemnify against covered claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 requires HDI to indemnify and hold harmless from covered claims and resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses.

elements.element: Customer is protected by Vendor's defense and indemnity.
elements.evidence: The Company is expressly an indemnitee under Section 9A.1.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are protected by Vendor's defense and indemnity.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly covers the Company’s affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity applies to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly applies to “any third party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims alleging that the services or Vendor-provided deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) covers allegations that the Site, HDI’s services, or materials, software or technology provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets or other IP rights.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(b) covers HDI’s breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers data breaches caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content, Confidential Information, or user or customer data caused by HDI.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(d) expressly covers HDI’s gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(d) expressly covers HDI’s willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 requires prompt written notice and provides that deficient notice relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent materially prejudiced.

elements.element: The indemnifying party controls the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 permits the indemnifying party to control defense and settlement, subject to consent for settlements imposing obligations or admissions on the indemnified party.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 requires reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party’s expense.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party IP claims based on Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 covers third-party IP claims concerning Content or Marks furnished by the Company and used by HDI in accordance with the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer indemnifies Vendor for claims arising from Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 covers the Company’s breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity contains no substantive triggers beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 contains only the Customer-furnished Content/Marks IP trigger and the Company breach-of-law trigger.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer for third-party IP infringement or misappropriation claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) provides this IP indemnity for the Site, HDI services, and HDI-provided materials, software and technology.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion addresses modifications made by the Company.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer combinations involving the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No exclusion addresses combinations made or supplied by the Company.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion addresses designs, instructions or specifications supplied by the Company.

elements.element: The IP remedies permit Vendor to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected service or deliverable.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no procure-rights remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies permit Vendor to modify the affected service or deliverable to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies permit Vendor to replace the affected service or deliverable with a non-infringing equivalent.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies require an appropriate refund if the affected service or deliverable cannot be procured, modified or replaced.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity obligations are subject to a super-cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no liability cap applicable to HDI’s indemnity obligations.

elements.element: The Vendor indemnity super-cap equals three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No three-times-annual-fees cap appears in the rendered language.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position, including all Vendor triggers, protected parties, procedures, and the narrow reciprocal Customer indemnity. It does not satisfy the fallback because it omits all specified IP exclusions, remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. The amendment preserves the existing commercial language, but it is not strictly minimal because it additionally extends protection to officers, directors and employees and adds hold-harmless and reciprocal defense duties beyond the stated requirements. Drafting quality is materially impaired by placing newly numbered Section 9A after the heading for Section 10, creating a significant structural and numbering defect.
